title: Rectangular prism
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and a translation vector of zero, zero, and zero. On the first face, draw the first loop consisting of six lines. Start by drawing the first line from the origin (zero, zero) to (zero point zero three three nine, zero). Continue with the second line from (zero point zero three three nine, zero) to (zero point zero three three nine, zero point zero three three nine). Draw the third line from (zero point zero three three nine, zero point zero three three nine) to (zero point zero three one nine, zero point zero three three nine). The fourth line goes from (zero point zero three one nine, zero point zero three three nine) to (zero point zero three one nine, zero point zero zero two). Draw the fifth line from (zero point zero three one nine, zero point zero zero two) to (zero, zero point zero zero two), and finish with the sixth line from (zero, zero point zero zero two) back to the origin. Scale the entire two-dimensional sketch by a factor of zero point zero three three nine. Rotate the scaled two-dimensional sketch using the same Euler angles as the coordinate system and translate it using the same translation vector. Extrude the two-dimensional sketch zero point seven five units along the normal direction without extruding in the opposite direction. Create a new solid body from this extrusion. The final dimensions of the rectangular prism are length zero point zero three three nine three six six five one five eight three seven one zero four one units, width zero point zero three three nine three six six five one five eight three seven one zero four one units, and height zero point seven five units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0339, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0339, 0.0339) \
     .lineTo(0.0319, 0.0339) \
     .lineTo(0.0319, 0.002) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.002) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0339, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0339, 0.0339) \
     .lineTo(0.0318, 0.0339) \
     .lineTo(0.0318, 0.0021) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0021) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The translation vector is [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], so no translation is needed

# Final model
r = r

lanes.label: GLM-5.3 Flash (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# L-angle profile dimensions
leg = 0.0339      # leg length in Y and Z
t = 0.0075        # material thickness
length = 0.7500   # extrusion length along X

# Build the L-profile in the YZ plane and extrude along X
r = (
    cq.Workplane("YZ")
    .moveTo(0.0, 0.0)
    .lineTo(leg, 0.0)
    .lineTo(leg, t)
    .lineTo(t, t)
    .lineTo(t, leg)
    .lineTo(0.0, leg)
    .close()
    .extrude(length)
)

lanes.label: Kimi K3 (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

L = 0.7500     # length along X
W = 0.0339     # leg width along Y
H = 0.0339     # leg height along Z
T = 0.0050     # angle thickness

# Equal-leg L-angle cross-section in the Y-Z plane, extruded along X.
# Outer corner is at (Y=W, Z=0); inner notch is toward low-Y/high-Z.
r = (
    cq.Workplane("YZ")
    .polyline([
        (0.0, 0.0),
        (W, 0.0),
        (W, H),
        (W - T, H),
        (W - T, T),
        (0.0, T),
    ])
    .close()
    .extrude(L)
)
